summary.body: Comment-only change, no behavior modification as intended. The new comment accurately describes the `n > len(items)` case, but the docstring/comment is incomplete: it doesn't mention the `n == 0` edge case, which is arguably the most surprising one. `items[-n:]` with `n == 0` evaluates to `items[0:]` (the whole list), not an empty list as most callers would intuitively expect from a function named `last_n`. Since the whole point of this PR is to document `last_n`'s edge-case behavior, silently omitting the `n == 0` quirk leaves the comment only partially trustworthy — a reader could reasonably assume all edge cases are now covered when they aren't.

items.markdown: The added comment documents the `n > len(items)` behavior but omits the `n == 0` case, where `items[-0:]` is `items[0:]` — the full list, not an empty one. This is the more counter-intuitive edge case for a function called `last_n`, and since this PR's stated purpose is to document edge-case behavior, leaving it out makes the comment incomplete/misleading about coverage.
